title: Style sample: science-atlas
objective: Show what a science-atlas film looks like: one specimen at true scale, opened rather than swapped, with a live scale bar.
audience: The Motion Lab team, reviewing what each style template looks like before using it.

message.core_message: Earth's crust is a thin skin, and our deepest hole reaches about 0.2% of the way to the centre.
key_points: Sets the object and its scale.
Names the four parts the film reuses.
Shows how thin the crust is at true scale.

constraints: Silent: no narration, music or effects; the picture carries it.
Built to style template science-atlas v1; scene roles follow its scene grammar.

research.reason: Style sample for look review, not a release. On-screen facts are a few well-established figures checked by hand; the source is named on screen. Radii: mean 6,371 km, core-mantle boundary 2,890 km deep, inner core 1,221 km; Kola borehole 12,262 m (1989).

creative_directions.name: science-atlas template
creative_directions.concept: A 22-second walk through the science-atlas template's scene grammar on a subject that fits its visual job: Inside the Earth, to scale.

composition.approach: Portrait only: copy in the top band, the hero in the middle, captions above the bottom UI zone.

creative_directions.pacing: A planned visual event at least every 2 seconds.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: It is the template's own grammar, so the sample shows the template rather than one film's choices.

success_criteria: Each scene role of the template is recognisable
No frame holds still for more than 2.5 s
